web_checks.title: The Indus Script(IM77) [HTML title]; in-app heading 'TEXTS, CONCORDANCE AND TABLES (IM77/IDF80)'
web_checks.contents: Flutter web application; the HTML is a loader shell and all content is in main.dart.js (3,550,289 bytes, Last-Modified 30 Sep 2021, sha256 5861d053...ff687b, not retained) with a Firebase/Firestore backend (project id 'theindusscript'). Strings extracted from the bundle state that RMRL, with support of the Department of Archaeology, Govt. of Tamil Nadu, publishes Mahadevan's updated corpus IM77/IDF80; that 'the texts and concordance are made available along with statistics pertaining to pairs and triplets'; and that IDF80 improved the categorization of field symbols. The bundle contains a sign concordance view, field-symbol descriptions, site groupings including 'Other Sites & West Asian Finds', Mahadevan's introduction and an obituary text. AssetManifest.json lists 418 numbered sign images in each of .jpg and .png plus field-symbol icons; no object photographs are bundled as assets. No object or text counts were found in the extracted strings. Counts from a secondary source (harappa.com blog, opened, item 2 witness): Mahadevan 'gathered 2,906 inscribed objects', 417 signs; IDF-80 adds five late texts, giving 419 signs 'across 2,911 objects in total'.
web_checks.access_route: Public URL in a browser. App text: 'No signup is required for the application. If you already have a gmail/google account, you can login using those details' (Firebase Google sign-in; browsing without login not tested). The client can generate PDFs ('Loading images for PDF creation..'). No documented export or API. Bundle links to https://rmrl.in/wp-content/uploads/IM77-Manual.pdf and intro.pdf both returned HTTP 404; /privacypolicy.html returns the same SPA shell (identical sha256).
web_checks.reuse_terms: not stated (no licence or terms string found in extracted bundle strings); rights-unverified. In-app citation: 'Mahadevan, Iravatham & Roja Muthiah Research Library (2021), The Indus Script Web Application(IM77/IDF80). https://indusscript.in'
metadata_it_would_add: identity/aliases: IM77 text numbers, IDF80 codes (per app descriptors 'IDF80 code (Input Data File 1980)')
object type and field symbol (IDF80 categories)
not seen at record level: dimensions, material, stratum, accession, images of objects
web_checks.notes: Maintainer per RMRL IRC page: 'developed by the Indus Research Centre' with 'funding support from the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology'. Record-level content was not inspected because the app must be run in a browser; Firestore was not queried directly.

web_checks.title: Indus Research Centre (section heading); subsection 'Iravatham Mahadevan Chair'
web_checks.contents: IRC started 2007 under Iravatham Mahadevan; R. Balakrishnan is honorary consultant. Links tngraffiti.in and IndusScript.in. The Iravatham Mahadevan (IM) Chair 'was established ... in 2025 by the Government of Tamil Nadu'. Planned activities listed: 'Creating a new, expanded Indus concordance'; annual Iravatham Mahadevan Memorial Lecture; a biannual journal titled Journal of Indus Studies; research in script, linguistics and ancient Tamil literature; translating the Indus knowledge corpus into Tamil; outreach; courses. No date, scope or status is given for the expanded concordance. Extracted page text is identical to the 2026-10-02 witness (data/raw/2026-10-02-dataset-landscape/witnesses-v1/rmrl-irc.html), although the HTML bytes differ. harappa.com blog 'An Indus Concordance and Tamil Potsherds, Now Online' (opened; undated, written in 2026 since it says the chair was endowed 'Last year') states: 'Its first stated project is a new and expanded concordance.' RMRL /en/events and /en/publications pages list no Indus concordance release.
web_checks.reuse_terms: '© 2026 Roja Muthiah Research Library. All rights reserved.'
metadata_it_would_add: none yet: the expanded concordance is announced as planned, with no release found
web_checks.notes: January 2025 news snippets (not opened) report a Rs 2 crore allocation for the chair announced with the prize (item 14).

web_checks.item: 4 ICIT, Interactive Corpus of Indus Texts
web_checks.title: Indus Writing [HTML title]; 'Interactive Corpus of Indus Text (ICIT)'
web_checks.contents: Landing page is byte-identical (sha256 2ec75bc7...) to the 2026-10-02 witness. It describes the database as developed by Bryan K. Wells and Andreas Fuls, with software by Fuls, and lists publications using ICIT. A linked page, video_2025_09_11.htm, embeds 'Fuls_Andreas_IndusScript_audiofile.mp4' under the link text 'Video: Bridging the gap between archaeology, epigraphy, and linguistics of the Indus script' (video not played). Counts: none newer than the CAA 2023 abstract were found. CAA 2023 abstract (local witness data/raw/2026-10-02-dataset-landscape/witnesses-v1/caa2023.pdf p.281): 4,665 inscribed objects, 5,650 texts, 17,966 legible sign occurrences, 16,015 images; relational database with 29 tables. Older: 2021 Digital Classicist seminar notice (opened): 4,537 inscribed objects, 5,509 texts, 19,616 sign occurrences. Sign list: ICIT documentation (2010, opened) says the Wells (2006) list 'contains 676 signs'; harappa.com review of Fuls 2023 says 'some 700'; a ResearchGate snippet (not opened) says 713 signs as of May 2023.
web_checks.access_route: Database URL http://www.indus.epigraphica.de returns HTTP 401. Page text: 'Ask the administrator (email: fuls(at)epigraphica.de) to get access to the database.' Documentation (help_onlinedatabase.pdf, 2010): two logins; guest access limited to 10 data; registration through the administrator.
metadata_it_would_add: identity/aliases: ICIT ID, CISI number, excavation number (per CAA 2023 abstract)
web_checks.notes: No data paper, export or public dump found. harappa.com blog (2026) describes the database as 'not open, but can be accessed by scholars and is largely based on the CISI volumes'.
